//: DECLARED ASSERTION-RECEIPT PROTOCOL, PER SUITE. Lands at web/test-receipts.manifest.json.
WHY A MANIFEST AND NOT SNIFFING. The two branches independently invented
assertion-count pinning with incompatible conventions, and a third convention
will arrive eventually. A runner that SNIFFS the output picks whichever format
it happens to recognise and treats an unrecognised one as absence -- which is
the exact shape of the #103 defect, one level up: a suite that reports nothing
and a suite whose report was not understood become indistinguishable, and the
quiet one wins. Declaring the protocol per suite makes a new convention a
REVIEWED LINE IN A DIFF instead of a silent reclassification.
DEFAULT. A suite absent from `suites` below must use the `receipt` protocol:
it imports src/util/assertions.ts, which prints `#assertions N` on exit. A
suite that is absent here AND emits no receipt is a HARD ERROR naming the
suite. It is never read as zero.
THE HAZARD IN `private-total`, STATED PLAINLY. This protocol matches a line of
the suite's own prose. That is a weaker contract than `receipt`: reword the
sentence and the match is lost. That failure is LOUD by construction -- a
declared private-total suite that emits no matching line is an error, not a
pass -- but it will be a confusing error, and the fix is to reword the pattern
here in the same commit. It is accepted deliberately: the alternative was to
rewrite a 5583-line suite's reporting to satisfy a runner, and a harness must
not get to rewrite the tests it is supposed to be checking.

why: web/src/util/markdown.test.ts line 5580. The suite keeps a private
`assertions` counter and self-checks it against its own
EXPECTED_ASSERTIONS (131 at that SHA, moved 127 -> 131 in round 10) and
against a computed EXPECTED_CHECKS. It emits no `#assertions` receipt:
It is declared rather than converted because its internal pin is already
the stronger check -- it fails on a count change with a message naming
which of the two totals moved -- and because converting it would mean
editing a suite this task has no mandate to touch.

aggregateAssertionPin_why: UNSET, DELIBERATELY, AND THIS IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT.
The XSS runner pinned `EXPECTED_ASSERTIONS = 380` as an exact equality over
the sum of all receipts. That number is not transferable to the reconciled
suite: the union adds util/markdown (131 assertions by its own count) and the
shared utils/task-ready.test.ts exists as two different blobs with different
assertion counts, so the correct total depends on a merge that has not
happened and on a run that has not been authorised.
SETTING IT BY ARITHMETIC WOULD BE A GUESS WEARING A MEASUREMENT'S CLOTHES.
380 + 131 is a plausible-looking number that no one has observed, and a pin
asserted at a wrong value is worse than an absent one: it goes red on a
correct tree, and the person who clears it will clear it by editing the pin,
which trains everyone to edit the pin.
WHAT IS UNPROTECTED WHILE THIS IS NULL: a count-neutral or count-reducing
change INSIDE a suite that still runs. Deleting one assertion from a suite
that still evaluates two hundred is invisible until this is set. What is
still protected: every suite's own internal pin (util/markdown's 131), the
per-suite zero/no-receipt gates, and suite MEMBERSHIP via test-suites.pin.
Membership is the #103 defect; this pin is a different and narrower one.
TO SET IT: run the reconciled suite once on the merged tree, take the printed
total, and commit it here with the SHA it was measured at. The runner prints
the exact line to paste. It must be MEASURED, by someone holding the build
token -- not derived, not carried over from either branch.
